name: config_resource_rename

preconditionToken.nativeLocation: none: the documented rename route takes no signature parameter
preconditionToken.raceWindow: D30 §2: the read-compare cannot be atomic with the dispatch, so a competing writer inside the window changes the resource the rename applies to. Nothing here claims otherwise.

targetId.collection: the default configuration collection only: the Target allowlist names a resource, so a caller-supplied collection is refused with invalid_argument
targetId.denialCodeSource: D30 §7, Tool-scoped; the Phase 3 machinery keeps operation_disabled

targets: <resourceType>/<name>: the resource being renamed, whose state the rename changes
targetIds.rule: D30 §3 Preflight: every Target a call changes is checked before anything executes, so both are checked and both must be allowlisted. A rename never applies to a singleton (its type has no documented rename route).
targetIds.openQuestion: D30 does not state the Target rule for a *config* rename. The Runtime rule for `tag_rename` names only the new path; the more conservative reading is taken here, and the runbook records it as an open question for the owner.

requestSchemaValidation.schema: the documented rename request body, bundled into a self-contained JSON Schema (internal $refs hoisted to $defs) at capability refresh time
requestSchemaValidation.appliesTo: the complete rename body, before dispatch
requestSchemaValidation.unavailableDisposition: a documented rename route without a usable request schema exposes no rename route, so the Tool refuses the resource type with unsupported_capability

collisionPolicy: D11: an occupied destination is a `conflict`. It is checked against the Gateway before dispatch, so a collision never consumes the caller's Resource signature, and a destination that appears in the race window is refused by the Gateway itself.

rejectionPolicy.rule: D30 §2: an explicit Gateway rejection is the result of the attempt — a 4xx (including 409 for an occupied destination, which D30 §7 maps to `conflict`) or a 2xx carrying success=false with a problem. No read-back may turn it into a success: a resource may have been moved by another writer.
verificationMaySucceedWhen: the Gateway claimed success (2xx with no refusal)
rejectionPolicy.ambiguousAttribution: a competing writer cannot be ruled out for an ambiguous dispatch, so a read-back that shows the resource at the new name is outcome_unknown, never a success; the old name still holding the caller's signature is not_applied

verification: bounded re-read of both names: the claimed success is confirmed only when the old name is vacant *and* the new name holds the resource, whose read-back is reported as Observed state
